solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: That is a sign of penitence, in a way (8)

indicatorNotes.in: the sign of penitence goes in the way

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a cilice is a hair shirt, worn as penance

annotation.surface: Someone explaining a gesture of remorse.
annotation.walkthrough: "That is" reads as the start of a sentence, but it is the definition: scilicet is Latin for "namely", shortened to sc.
annotation.definitionFit: Scilicet means "that is to say" or "namely", used to introduce an explanation.

entries.clue: Corpse in one rotten state (7)

blocks.note: a cad is a rotter, a dishonourable man
to aver is to state firmly

annotation.surface: A body found in a decomposing condition.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rotten state" suggests decay to go with the corpse; "state" is a verb, and "one rotten" is a rotter.
annotation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a dead body, especially one used for dissection.

entries.clue: Border I’m filling in (5)

indicatorNotes.filling: I'M fills the middle of the other word

blocks.note: a fire that is still in is lit
I'm as written, without the apostrophe

annotation.surface: Someone filling in a border, as in a colouring book or form.
annotation.walkthrough: "Filling in" reads as one phrase; split it, and "in" means alight, as when you ask if the fire is still in.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a border marks where something stops, its boundary.

entries.clue: Having beef, vanilla slices next (11)

indicatorNotes.slices: vanilla slices into the other word, cutting it open

blocks.note: coming, as in "the coming week"
vanilla means plain, ordinary

annotation.surface: A menu: beef, followed by vanilla slices for pudding.
annotation.walkthrough: A vanilla slice is a British custard pastry, and beef sits beside it like a menu; but beef is slang for a grievance, and "slices" is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a beef is slang for a grievance, so someone having one is grumbling about it.

entries.clue: Its art is not laid out in squares (15)

indicatorNotes.laid out: the letters are laid out in a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 15 letters

annotation.surface: A remark about an abstract painting that ignores the grid.
annotation.walkthrough: "Squares" looks like a grid for the art; it is the definition, squares being old-fashioned people.
annotation.definitionFit: Squares are conventional, old-fashioned people, as traditionalists are.

entries.clue: Car maker left out of TLS book reviews? (6)

indicatorNotes.out of: the L is taken out of TLS

blocks.note: Audi is a German car maker
TLS with L (left) removed

annotation.surface: A car manufacturer dropped from the Times Literary Supplement's pages.
annotation.walkthrough: The TLS is the Times Literary Supplement, which does review books; here the books are accounts, and the question mark flags the twist.
annotation.definitionFit: An audit is a review of an organisation's books, its financial accounts.

entries.clue: I am willing to give it back (3)

blocks.clueFragment: I am willing to give it
blocks.note: a common saying with its last two words left off; those two words, run together, are the entry
back in time, as in "years back"

annotation.surface: Someone agreeing to return something.
annotation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: finish the saying "I am willing to give it ..." with A GO, then read those letters as one word meaning back.
annotation.definitionFit: Ago means back in time, as in "ten years ago" or "ten years back".

entries.clue: A country boy upset about a famous exile (5,4)

indicatorNotes.about: the boy's letters go round the second A
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns everything upside down

blocks.note: A as written
Mali is a West African country
a as written
a lad is a boy

annotation.surface: A country boy upset by the story of a famous exile.
annotation.walkthrough: "Upset" reads as the boy's mood; in a down clue it turns the whole assembly upside down, and "about a" means the lone a sits inside, not a topic of conversation.
annotation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama, the Tibetan spiritual leader, has lived in exile in India since 1959.

entries.clue: A little node protecting upturned sea shell? (7)

indicatorNotes.A little: only a little of the clue's text is used
indicatorNotes.upturned: in a down clue, upturned means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run through "n(ODE PROT)ecting"

annotation.surface: A shell guarding a small knob, like a seashell on the beach.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sea shell" suggests the beach; the question mark flags a shell in the military sense, fired under the sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater missile, a shell that travels through the sea.

entries.clue: An embankment’s architect (4)

blocks.note: an = a
a barrier or bank holding back water

annotation.surface: Asking who designed an embankment.
annotation.walkthrough: Robert Adam was an 18th-century Scottish architect, famous for neoclassical houses.
annotation.definitionFit: Robert Adam is the architect; the definition names him by his job.

entries.clue: One bird giving me a secret about another (10)

indicatorNotes.about: the secret goes round the other bird

blocks.note: me as written
a as written
to keep something dark is to keep it secret
another bird: an owl

annotation.surface: One bird telling another bird's secret.
annotation.walkthrough: "Another" means another bird, taken from "One bird" at the start.
annotation.definitionFit: The meadowlark is a North American songbird.

entries.clue: Sex talk almost crucial (5)

indicatorNotes.almost: the word is not quite complete: its last letter goes

blocks.note: sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals
TALK without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone insisting that talking about sex is important.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sex" is Latin for six, so it gives the numeral VI; nothing to do with the surface topic.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something without which a thing cannot live or work is both.

entries.clue: Felt I tuned it badly (8)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are put together badly, in the wrong order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A musician admitting they tuned an instrument poorly.
annotation.walkthrough: "Felt" looks like a noun, the material of a piano hammer; it is the verb, sensed.
annotation.definitionFit: To intuit something is to feel or sense it without reasoning.

entries.clue: New artillery parts for a wife / attorney (5,6)

indicatorNotes.New: the letters are made into a new word
indicatorNotes.parts for: the new word parts to let the other letters in

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
a as written
W is the abbreviation for wife

annotation.surface: Fresh artillery pieces ordered for an attorney's wife.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram of ARTILLERY opens after TRIALL to take A and W.
annotation.definitionFit: A trial lawyer is an attorney who argues cases in court, chiefly an American term.

entries.clue: I’m into this, interrupting sadly prostrate conjuror (15)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: the phrase breaks into the middle of the other word

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
"I dig it" is slang for I'm into this, I like it

annotation.surface: A fan cheering on a conjuror who lies face down in a trick.
annotation.walkthrough: "I'm into this" has to be rephrased as the slang "I dig it"; those letters sit after PREST in the anagram of PROSTRATE.
annotation.definitionFit: A prestidigitator is a conjuror who relies on sleight of hand.

entries.clue: Joker — turn over to show face (5,2,2)

blocks.note: a stand-up is a stand-up comic, a joker
TO is the abbreviation for turn over, as in PTO

annotation.surface: A card game: turn over the Joker to show its face.
annotation.walkthrough: The Joker suggests a playing card turned face up; it is a comedian, and "face" means confront.
annotation.definitionFit: To stand up to someone is to face them down, confront them.

entries.clue: Part-time board member? (10,5)

blocks.note: part-time work is occasional
a board is a table, as in bed and board

annotation.surface: A company director who only turns up now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: "Board member" suggests a director; read it as a member of the board family, a table, and one only used now and then.
annotation.definitionFit: An occasional table is a small table brought out when needed, so a board used part-time.

entries.clue: Train to have wheels in middle (7)

indicatorNotes.wheels: the word wheels round, turning back on itself
indicatorNotes.in: the turned word goes in the middle

blocks.note: the core is the middle
to get is to have or receive

annotation.surface: A train needing wheels in the middle carriages.
annotation.walkthrough: "Train" suggests a railway and "wheels" fits; a train is also a procession, and "wheels" says turn round.
annotation.definitionFit: A cortege is a procession, especially at a funeral, and a train can mean a line of followers.

entries.clue: 50 per cent left with room to fill grid (7)

indicatorNotes.50 per cent: only half of the word is used
indicatorNotes.to fill: the room fills the gap inside the half-word

blocks.note: half of LEFT
an attic is a room in the roof

annotation.surface: Half the space is left, with a room still to fill on a floor plan.
annotation.walkthrough: "Left" is not L here but the whole word LEFT, halved to LE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: crossed strips of wood or metal with square or diamond gaps form a grid.

entries.clue: Excessive butt on one girl (8)

blocks.note: to butt is to push or prod
I is the Roman numeral for one
gal is informal for girl

annotation.surface: Complaining about too much bottom on show from a girl.
annotation.walkthrough: "Butt" reads as a noun, a bottom; it is the verb, as a goat butts.
annotation.definitionFit: Prodigal means wastefully extravagant, excessive.

entries.clue: Sweep a little to hide marks (5)

indicatorNotes.to hide: the letter is hidden inside the phrase

blocks.note: a little = a bit
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

annotation.surface: Sweeping lightly to cover up stains.
annotation.walkthrough: "Sweep" looks like housework; it is a noun meaning range or scope.
annotation.definitionFit: An ambit is the scope or extent of something, its sweep.

entries.clue: Bowled, eg, bowl (5)

blocks.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
eg = for example = as in

annotation.surface: A cricket note: bowled, for example, meaning to bowl.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket scoring, B means bowled, a batsman dismissed by the ball hitting the wicket.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a round open container for washing or mixing, as in a pudding basin.

entries.clue: Without power, playing Shelley’s covers album (10)

indicatorNotes.playing: the letters play about into a new order
indicatorNotes.covers: the new word covers the album, going round it

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters
an LP is a long-playing record, an album

annotation.surface: During a power cut, someone playing Pete Shelley's covers album.
annotation.walkthrough: Pete Shelley was the singer of the Buzzcocks; "covers album" suggests a record of other people's songs, but "covers" is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: acting with no power to change things, unable to help yourself.

entries.clue: Close friends, to some extent (3)

indicatorNotes.to some extent: only some of the word is used

blocks.note: the letters sit in the middle of this word, between its first three letters and its last

annotation.surface: Describing how near to each other some friends are.
annotation.walkthrough: "Close" reads as the adjective, as in close friends; it is the noun, the end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the close of a day or a story is its finish.

entries.clue: Match action (4)

blocks.note: to go well with, as colours do
a case brought in a court of law

annotation.surface: A sports report calling for action in a game.
annotation.walkthrough: "Action" here is the legal sense, a case brought in court.
annotation.definitionFit: Suit means both to match and a lawsuit.

entries.clue: After that, sleeping? (6)

indicatorNotes.sleeping?: someone sleeping is in bed, so the word goes inside BED

blocks.note: a sleeper is in bed
yon is old-fashioned for that, as in "yon hill"

annotation.surface: Wondering what comes after sleep, perhaps after death.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that "sleeping" is a picture: THAT (yon) is in bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the preposition: later than, or on the far side of, as in past the deadline.

entries.clue: Not a word published — knowledge wasted (8)

blocks.note: sh! means be quiet, not a word
a story run in a paper is published
ken is knowledge, as in beyond my ken

annotation.surface: An author lamenting that nothing got published and all their learning came to nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: The pieces are all short: SH, RUN and KEN, a Scottish word for knowledge.
annotation.definitionFit: Wasted can mean withered or emaciated, which is shrunken.
